- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at +2–4% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 5 days, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- In low-sentiment periods (sentiment < 0.33 for 5+ days), model underperforms; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to compensate for lack of momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below model (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for next 3–5 days to avoid overconfidence bias.
